newsitem.title: USA: World silver output seen rising led by Australia.
newsitem.headline: World silver output seen rising led by Australia.

text.p: Silver miners are projecting production increases for each year through to 1999, reversing the trend of the early 1990s, according to the Silver Institute's just published annual "World Silver Production Forecast".

Although not matching 1995's six percent gain, producers expect a two percent output increase in 1996 to 478.6 million ounces, a four percent and five percent rise in 1997 and 1998 respectively, followed by a three percent rise in 1999, bringing 1999's total silver output to 541.4 million ounces, the report said.
If projections are met, Australian production will outpace U.S. output by 1999, making Australia the third largest global producer after Mexico and Peru, the institute said.

While Mexican silver production has hovered around 70 million ounces for the last 10 years, producers there expect to break significantly from that level, projecting increases of 25 percent over the next four years to 93.4 million ounces in 1999.
Silver production in Peru increased more than 14 percent in 1995 and is expected to rise another five percent by 1999 to 64.1 million ounces.
The world's third largest silver supplier, U.S. production is expected to increase 10 percent over the next four years, from 49.8 million ounces in 1995, to 54.8 million in 1999.

Four year projections for the CIS (former Soviet Union)-- a compilation of published data for Russia and data from the intitute's "World Silver Survey 1996" -- show generally flat production cycles through to 1999.

For Canada, where production jumped almost 70 percent last year, miners project an overall increase of nearly eight percent for the next four years, bringing the country's output to 41.9 million ounces by 1999.

Despite projected increases in all of the top silver producing countries, Australia leads the world in terms of projected expansion, forecasting an increase of 97 percent over the next four years, from 29.6 million ounces in 1995, to 58.3 million ounce in 1999.

While a number of mines are due to come onstream, the largest boost to Australian silver output is expected to come from the Carrington deposit in Queensland. Production forecasts for this facility are expected to reach 24 million ounces annually, the Silver Institute said.
The production forecasts were compiled by the Washington DC-based Silver Institute, with the participation of 106 mining entities supplying production data and projections.
